top_findings.description: Temporal cluster 14:00:50-14:04:07 UTC 2020-11-14 (197s, 3 independent sources: EVTX+file_system+registry, confidence 0.90) confirms the attacker's Outlook PST email exfiltration to Google Drive cloud. Three independent artifact streams co-occur within 4 minutes: EVTX records SharePoint/admin share access (F-050, F-096); file_system records Outlook PST file operations (F-100, F-105); and registry WordWheelQuery (F-112) records the search sequence *.pst → backup → backup.pst proving PST discovery methodology, with LastWrite 14:04:07 UTC. LNK and Jump List evidence confirms Outlook 2016 opened G:\My Drive\STARK-RESEARCH-LABS FOLDER\Exported-PST\SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst at 14:01:34 UTC and backup.pst at 14:03:52 UTC. The PST was subsequently deleted to Recycle Bin at 14:07:32 UTC (F-115). Google Drive File Stream auto-synced the exported PST to attacker-controlled cloud storage.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Fred performed a routine Outlook PST backup operation before departing on vacation, and the registry searches reflect his normal maintenance workflow.
evidence_against_it: Fred departed on 2020-11-10 (manifest), five days before this 2020-11-14 activity; the search sequence *.pst → backup → backup.pst (F-112) proves the PST filename was not known in advance and was discovered through enumeration, inconsistent with routine backup by the file owner; the PST was exported to G:\My Drive\...\Exported-PST\ (a new subdirectory) then deleted to Recycle Bin (F-115), not retained locally; the attacker-controlled srl-h account was the active session during this window per EVTX logon records

top_findings.description: Temporal cluster 03:42:49-03:46:33 UTC 2020-11-14 (224s, 4 independent sources: EVTX+MFT+file_system+Prefetch, confidence 0.95) confirms the attacker's active SRL IP data collection and physical exfiltration window. Four independent artifact streams co-occur: EVTX records system activity (F-048); MFT records file system writes/reads (F-043); ShellBags/LNK records Explorer navigation to SRL project folders (F-072); and Prefetch records program execution (F-101, F-102). LNK files confirm the attacker accessed ADAMANTIUM-Background.docx (03:43), Airwolf project files (03:43-03:47), and began copying to CRIMSON2 USB (F:\Files of interest\) during this window. The 4-source convergence on a 4-minute window with no legitimate user (Fred departed 2020-11-10) rules out Fred's routine use.
top_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Fred or another authorized SRL user remotely accessed the laptop during this window and performed routine file operations.
evidence_against_it: Fred was confirmed absent on vacation since 2020-11-10 (manifest); srl-h account (not Fred's account fredr) was the active session per EVTX logon records; CRIMSON2 USB device (removable, non-SRL-issued) was mounted during this window per LNK file evidence (F-101); Google Drive File Stream was syncing SRL project files to external cloud during this window

top_findings.description: Recycle Bin contains four post-exfiltration cleanup events establishing the attacker's cleanup sequence: (1) backup.pst ($IDNBREY.pst) deleted at 2020-11-14 14:07:32 UTC — original path C:\Users\fredr\OneDrive\Documents\Outlook Files\backup.pst, size 20,587,520 bytes (20.6 MB), content still present; (2) sdelete.exe ($I9531FE.exe) deleted at 13:41:24 UTC — original path C:\Users\fredr\Downloads\SDelete\sdelete.exe, size 235,560 bytes, content still present (anti-forensics tool not securely self-wiped); (3) Downloads folder bulk cleanup at 04:49:53–04:50:11 UTC: Windows10Upgrade9252.exe (6.2 MB), DropboxInstaller.exe, GrammarlyAddInSetup.exe (14.8 MB), installbackupandsync(1).exe, ZoomOutlookPluginSetup.msi (7.6 MB) all sent to Recycle Bin. All 19 Recycle Bin entries have content_present=True — no SDelete secure-wipe was applied to any Recycle Bin entry, meaning the $R payload files (including backup.pst content) remain forensically recoverable. The cleanup sequence was: mass-delete Downloads installers (04:50) → delete BitLocker key (12:48) → delete sdelete.exe (13:41) → delete backup.pst (14:07).

Recycle Bin entry $IDNBREY.pst proves the BitLocker recovery key file was found on Fred's OneDrive Desktop and deleted to the Recycle Bin at 2020-11-14 12:48:13 UTC. Original path: C:\Users\fredr\OneDrive\Desktop\BitLocker Recovery Key 26F77152-999C-45E8-8BD4-C83FAC7BB72D.TXT, original_size_bytes: 1348, content_present: True ($R82PUWF.TXT still on disk, key content is forensically recoverable). This directly corroborates the WordWheelQuery evidence (F-112) showing Explorer searches for "bitlocker" and "bitlocker recovery key", confirming the attacker found the key on Fred's OneDrive-synced Desktop and accessed/exfiltrated it before deleting it at 12:48:13 UTC. The key ID 26F77152-999C-45E8-8BD4-C83FAC7BB72D is associated with a BitLocker-protected volume in the SRL environment. The OneDrive Desktop sync means the key file was accessible via Fred's OneDrive account from any authenticated device — its exposure extends beyond this laptop. URGENT: SRL must rotate/replace all BitLocker volumes protected by this recovery key immediately.

Edge browser download record at 04:13:22 UTC proves a file from Maria Hill's private SharePoint OneDrive was downloaded directly to the CRIMSON2 USB drive. Source URL: https://starkresearchlabs-my.sharepoint.com/personal/mhill_stark-research-labs_com/Documents/Quantum%20Particles%20Affected%20by%20Other%20Dimensions.pdf. Target path: F:\Files from SRL system\Quantum Particles Affected by Other Dimensions.pdf (153,290 bytes). The referrer headers in the download record (OR=Outlook-Body, CID=5CF3E828-0DA2-4E7E-8E26-AF4853DB96A0) indicate the attacker clicked a link inside an Outlook email body to reach mhill's SharePoint file. Prior page visit at 04:12:52 UTC showed the attacker was redirected to mhill's OneDrive via a shared link. This is definitive proof of browser-mediated direct-to-USB exfiltration of a colleague's private SharePoint document, corroborating F-106 (mhill SharePoint access via Office applications).

top_findings.description: Browser history (Chrome) proves SDelete was searched and downloaded by the attacker during the 2020-11-14 attack session. At 13:37:37 UTC Chrome shows Google search for "sdelete download"; at 13:37:47 visited docs.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/sdelete; two download records at 13:37:51 and 13:38:02 UTC both write SDelete.zip (226,573 bytes) to C:\Users\fredr\Downloads\SDelete.zip from the Microsoft Docs page. This confirms SDelete was freshly downloaded 10 seconds after visiting the download page — in addition to the srl-h sdelete64.exe pre-staged 24 days earlier (same SHA-1: 7bcd946326b67f806b3db4595ede9fbdf29d0c36). The attacker downloaded SDelete under fredr's account while the attack was in progress, establishing fresh anti-forensics tooling under the victim's credential trail.

Jump Lists confirm Microsoft Outlook 2016 was used to access both the local PST file (backup.pst) and the Google Drive PST (SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst). Outlook AppId (Microsoft Outlook 2016 64-bit) entry for backup.pst: C:\Users\fredr\OneDrive\Documents\Outlook Files\backup.pst, LastModified 2020-11-14 14:03:52, InteractionCount=1. Outlook AppId entry for SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst: G:\My Drive\STARK-RESEARCH-LABS FOLDER\Exported-PST\SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst (VolumeLabel: Google Drive File Stream), LastModified 2020-11-14 14:01:34, InteractionCount=1. Additionally, the Windows Explorer Jump List shows a search entry "Search Results in Windows (C:)&backup.pst" at 14:00:54 UTC — proving the attacker searched the entire C: drive for "backup.pst" before opening it, demonstrating deliberate targeting of the email archive. The Windows Explorer entry for the G:\Exported-PST folder has InteractionCount=2 (opened twice). This is the definitive proof that Outlook was used to open the PST files (not just file copy), enabling full email corpus access.

SDELETE.EXE executed 7 times across two paths during the attacker's session (13:42–13:47 UTC 2020-11-14). First 2 runs from Users\fredr\Downloads\SDelete\SDELETE.EXE (Prefetch hash -2BD91720) at 13:42:30 and 13:42:38 UTC; subsequent 5 runs with SDelete copied to Windows\System32\SDELETE.EXE (hash -0E837E93) at 13:44:52–13:47:10 UTC. The 0E837E93 Prefetch referenced_files list explicitly names the SRL IP documents targeted for secure deletion: EARTHFORCE SA-26 THUNDERBOLT STAR FURY.DOCX, EARTH_SA-26_THUNDERBOLT.JPG, ADAMANTIUM-BACKGROUND.DOCX, VIBRANIUM-ALLOY-RESULTS.DOCX, THE SHIELD BACKGROUND AND ONGOING RESEARCH.DOCX, NOKIA STRATEGY.DOCX, and BUSINESS_PLAN_MAIL_ORDER_PHARMACY*.DOCX. All targets resided in Users\fredr\OneDrive\ and Users\fredr\OneDrive\Desktop\.

top_findings.description: WordWheelQuery registry key (NTUSER.DAT, LastWriteTimestamp 2020-11-14 14:04:07 UTC) records 11 search terms typed into Windows Explorer's search bar, revealing the attacker's systematic intelligence-collection methodology in reverse MRU order: MRU:10 starfury, MRU:9 kitt, MRU:8 airwolf, MRU:7 crimson, MRU:6 cobra — targeted searches for SRL project names; MRU:5 bitlocker, MRU:4 bitlocker recovery key — the attacker searched for the system's BitLocker recovery key (corroborating srl-h's earlier BitLockerWizardElev.exe execution on 2020-10-20); MRU:3 sdelete — searched for the anti-forensics tool; MRU:2 *.pst — searched for ALL PST files on the system before targeting; MRU:1 backup, MRU:0 backup.pst — final targeted search for the email archive. The sequential progression from *.pst → backup → backup.pst proves the attacker discovered the email archive through a filesystem wildcard search, not prior knowledge of the filename. The BitLocker recovery key search indicates an attempt to decrypt BitLocker-protected volumes on the SRL network.

LNK file SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.lnk (SourceCreated 2020-11-14 14:01:35 UTC) definitively proves the Outlook PST export was placed on Google Drive File Stream as G:\My Drive\STARK-RESEARCH-LABS FOLDER\Exported-PST\SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst (VolumeLabel: Google Drive File Stream, VolumeSerial: 19831116). A companion LNK (backup.lnk, 14:03:52 UTC) confirms the local source was C:\Users\fredr\OneDrive\Documents\Outlook Files\backup.pst. This establishes the complete email exfiltration chain: Outlook exported to local backup.pst → copied/renamed to SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst on G:\ → Google Drive File Stream auto-synced the file to the cloud account → local backup.pst deleted to Recycle Bin ($RDNBREY.pst, 14:07 UTC) and then SDelete used to wipe originals. The cloud copy at G:\Exported-PST\SRL-EMAIL-EXPORT.pst is the exfiltrated artifact requiring Google account preservation.

top_confirmed_findings.alternative_hypothesis: Fred performed a routine Outlook PST backup operation before departing on vacation, and the registry searches reflect his normal maintenance workflow.
